title: Define metric governance, targets, and tolerance contracts
what: Let planning leaders configure and understand the business rules behind every management metric, then evaluate performance against agreed targets without changing the source-safe population contract.
criteria: Forecast accuracy is explicitly identified as the configured business formula, including denominator eligibility and negative-value behavior.
Accuracy, bias, revision-effectiveness, coverage, and forecast-completeness targets can be configured globally and overridden by hierarchy or horizon.
Every target-backed metric exposes actual value, target, variance, and an On target, Watch, or Off target status.
The dashboard provides a user-facing metric glossary with units, numerator, denominator, population rules, and zero-denominator behavior.
Refresh language distinguishes last successful refresh, data-current-through date, and period-close status instead of using an ambiguous live-data claim.
Target and glossary changes are validated against automated metric and browser fixtures.

title: Make analysis scopes saveable and shareable
what: Let a user preserve, reopen, and share the exact analytical population and view state used in a demand review.
criteria: The URL represents all shared population filters, selected tab, comparison subview, metric selectors, and selected product-target detail.
Opening a shared URL reconstructs the same population, counts, charts, and view without silently falling back to defaults.
Users can save a named view, rename it, delete it, and choose a default view.
Users can bookmark products or brands and return to recent analysis scopes.
Invalid or no-longer-available values produce an explicit recovery message while preserving the remaining valid scope.
Saved and shared scopes are covered by browser history, reload, and backward/forward tests.

title: Replace portfolio dropdowns with hierarchy-aware search and multi-select
what: Let users find and select large product populations quickly across business hierarchies without scrolling through long native dropdowns.
criteria: Brand and product controls support search-as-you-type and multi-selection while remaining keyboard accessible.
Users can navigate available category, brand, sub-brand, and parent-product hierarchy levels supplied by the dataset.
Users can paste a list of product codes and receive a clear matched, unmatched, and duplicate summary before applying it.
Recent and pinned products are available without changing the shared population contract.
Selection summaries remain compact at hundreds or thousands of selected members and expose the full list on demand.
Filtering, reset, empty states, exports, and responsive behavior remain correct with single and multiple selections.

title: Establish a chart readability and interaction standard
what: Give every analytical chart a consistent, meeting-safe contract for scales, units, dates, evidence, accessibility, and interaction.
criteria: Every quantitative chart shows explicit axis titles, units, readable ticks, and year-aware date labels where dates can repeat across years.
Signed metrics show a visible zero reference and use direction-preserving encodings rather than absolute bar length alone.
Actuals cutoff, closed periods, and forecast-only future periods are visibly distinguished.
Tooltips show the metric value, source, product or hierarchy context, period or horizon, actual volume, forecast volume, and eligible count where applicable.
Targets, tolerance bands, and materiality references use one consistent visual language.
Charts remain interpretable without hover in screenshots and meeting-room display conditions.
Keyboard, screen-reader, reduced-motion, contrast, zoom, and responsive tests cover the shared chart contract.

title: Deliver the director executive cockpit
what: Give a demand planning director a first screen that answers whether performance is on target, what changed, and what needs intervention now.
criteria: The primary KPI row contains forecast accuracy versus target, bias versus tolerance, absolute error or configured value at risk, and revision effectiveness or forecast value add.
Coverage and data trust remain visible without competing equally with the four management KPIs.
Rolling 3-month, rolling 12-month, prior-period, and prior-year comparisons are available when the selected population has sufficient history.
The page shows the top material risks, top improvement opportunities, and currently open actions from the active population.
A deterministic summary states the most important measured changes without asserting unsupported causes.
Population and formula audit detail remains available through progressive disclosure.
The cockpit passes director-scale readability, empty-state, and responsive browser validation.

title: Fix monthly forecast-versus-actual analysis
what: Let users compare forecast and actual volume honestly over time and connect volume variance to accuracy and bias performance.
criteria: Forecast versus actual renders two explicitly labeled, quantitatively comparable series rather than a forecast-only line with actuals available only in hover evidence.
The view exposes forecast-minus-actual variance in KL and percentage terms with correct zero-denominator handling.
Accuracy, bias, and absolute-error modes use explicit units and the same period population as the volume comparison.
Actuals cutoff and forecast-only future months are clearly marked and do not appear as unexplained blank chart space.
Users can choose monthly granularity, rolling windows, and prior-period or prior-year overlays when data supports them.
Zoom, brush, or range selection updates the selected period and can feed the active exception population.
Automated tests prove forecast and actual evidence remains aligned under filtering and comparison mode.

title: Upgrade horizon and brand-month diagnosis
what: Let users see where performance deteriorates by forecast horizon and hierarchy, with encodings that preserve sign, target, materiality, and sample context.
criteria: Horizon performance uses a labeled dot or line representation with a zero reference for signed metrics.
TM and ML can be compared side by side only at aligned horizons, with actual volume and observation counts available at each point.
Horizon-specific targets and target attainment are visible when configured.
The brand-by-target-month heatmap uses diverging scales for signed metrics, target-aware scales for accuracy, and sequential scales for magnitude metrics.
The heatmap displays a legend, year-aware month labels, robust outlier handling, and an explicit statement of how many brands and months are shown versus available.
Users can change the visible hierarchy depth and select a heatmap cell or horizon point for downstream investigation.
Tests cover negative accuracy, extreme bias, sparse cells, quality groups, and aligned source comparison.

title: Upgrade revision-effectiveness diagnosis
what: Let planning leaders understand when revisions add value, where they cause deterioration, and how revision behavior changes over time.
criteria: Improved, worsened, neutral, and unchanged outcomes show counts and percentages against clearly named denominators.
Revision effectiveness is trended over target month and can be decomposed by hierarchy and horizon.
A Pareto view identifies the products or segments responsible for most worsened-revision error.
The revision scatter has labeled axes, tick values, named quadrants, materiality references, and point evidence.
Dense populations support zoom and either lasso selection or a density/hexbin representation without hiding outliers.
Selecting an outcome, segment, or scatter region produces a matching observation set for investigation.
Revision tolerance and materially revised denominators remain consistent with the configured metric contract.

title: Turn TM-versus-ML into a decision view
what: Help a model-governance or planning leader decide where ML or TM performs materially better on an aligned common population.
criteria: The paired-error chart has labeled axes, readable scales, a diagonal equality reference, and a configurable materiality band for ties.
Large populations remain interpretable through suitable scaling, transparency, density, or aggregation without losing material outliers.
Users can segment winner results by hierarchy, horizon, volume tier, lifecycle, and other available governed dimensions.
The view shows winner counts, actual volume, absolute-error difference, accuracy difference, bias difference, and source-only coverage.
Source adoption evidence distinguishes statistical superiority from coverage gaps and avoids recommending one source on incomparable populations.
Selecting a point or segment exposes the corresponding products and target months.
Aligned-population and coverage tests protect against cross-source or cross-horizon leakage.

title: Deliver a production-grade product deep dive
what: Let a planner investigate one product-target combination through complete chronological forecast development, actual context, revisions, stability, and related events.
criteria: The default selection is either a representative material observation with positive actual and sufficient history or an explicit choose-an-exception state.
Product selection supports search, recent and pinned items, and previous or next exception navigation.
The history chart has a labeled y-axis, value evidence, source-distinct vintage lines, actual reference, and forecast-horizon context.
The page shows source-specific error, bias, forecast range, volatility, revision count, maximum revision, and insufficient-history rules.
Consecutive revisions are ordered chronologically and link their amount, direction, and error outcome.
Governed promotions, overrides, freeze dates, and other available events can be overlaid without claiming causality.
The selected product, target, and source scope survive reload, sharing, and drill-through.

title: Promote forecast exceptions into a portfolio work queue
what: Give planning teams a dedicated, prioritized portfolio queue for finding and triaging the forecast observations that matter most.
criteria: Forecast exceptions are a first-class destination rather than a secondary subview under Product history.
Columns are sortable, filterable, resizable where appropriate, and configurable through a column chooser with a sticky header.
The queue supports hierarchy-aware search, bulk selection, and ranking by actual volume, absolute error, deterioration, and configured business materiality.
A Pareto summary shows cumulative contribution to absolute error and identifies the concentration in the top 10 and top 20 observations or products.
Rows expose all required metric, vintage, pair, mapping, and source evidence and can open the corresponding product-target investigation.
Preview limits are clearly distinguished from total active rows, and exports contain exactly the complete active population and advertised audit columns.
Large-population performance and keyboard accessibility are validated.

title: Connect charts, quality exceptions, and tables to drill-down
what: Turn separate reports into one investigative workflow where every signal can open the relevant observation set or product detail without losing context.
criteria: Monthly points and selected ranges can open or filter the matching forecast exceptions.
Horizon points and heatmap cells open the matching scoped observations.
Revision and TM-versus-ML scatter selections open a linked table and selected product deep dive.
Quality exception examples and queue rows open the correct product-target context.
Back, forward, reload, and shared URLs preserve the originating scope and selected observation.
A visible breadcrumb or return action takes the user back to the originating analysis without resetting filters.
Cross-view browser tests prove counts and exports remain consistent after drill-through.

title: Turn Data quality into a compact Data trust workspace
what: Give directors, planners, and data stewards a concise view of whether the analysis is trustworthy and a focused path to remediate material data problems.
criteria: Hierarchy, actual, pair, source, forecast-completeness, and refresh states show count, percentage, affected products, affected periods, and actual-volume impact.
Data-current-through date, expected refresh SLA, last successful refresh, and refresh failures are visible.
Exception previews avoid repetitive rows by summarizing affected products first while preserving product-month detail on expansion.
Each issue category shows first-seen date, current status, remediation owner when available, and a category-specific export.
Severity reflects business impact and recency rather than treating every non-good state equally.
Technical provenance, source files, metric version, and processing details are consolidated in a Data and metric lineage drawer.
Director and data-steward presentations use the same facts at different density levels.

title: Add accountable exception-management workflow
what: Let teams assign, investigate, resolve, and audit material forecast exceptions without editing the forecast itself.
criteria: An exception can have an owner, status, due date, root-cause category, comment thread, agreed action, and expected impact.
Users can assign and update multiple selected exceptions in bulk with role-appropriate validation.
Resolution requires a disposition and supporting evidence; resolved items can be reopened with a recorded reason.
Overdue, unassigned, escalated, and repeatedly reopened items are visible as dedicated queue states.
Every workflow change records actor, timestamp, previous value, and new value in an audit history.
The director cockpit and product deep dive show related open actions without changing analytical metrics.
Workflow tests cover concurrency, permissions-ready ownership boundaries, and export of the current action state.

title: Add threshold alerts and subscriptions
what: Notify the right users when forecast performance, data trust, or exception workflow crosses an agreed management threshold.
criteria: Users can subscribe to governed alert rules at portfolio, hierarchy, product, source, and horizon scopes.
Supported rules include sustained bias, accuracy deterioration, material worsened revisions, missing actuals beyond SLA, lost source coverage, and overdue or unassigned actions.
Alerts state the triggering metric, threshold, population, evidence, and direct link to the relevant dashboard scope.
Deduplication and cooldown rules prevent repeated notifications for the same unresolved condition.
Users can acknowledge, mute, or unsubscribe within their permitted scope without altering the underlying exception.
Alert delivery and failure states are auditable and covered by deterministic rule tests.

title: Add the first end-to-end forecast-value-add stage comparison
what: Prove the forecast-value-add architecture with one complete comparison between a governed baseline forecast and the final approved forecast.
criteria: The analysis contract represents forecast stage separately from source and vintage without combining incompatible rows.
Baseline and final stages align on source-safe product-target populations and expose stage-only coverage.
The view reports accuracy, bias, absolute error, incremental error improvement, percentage improved, and material deterioration for each stage.
Users can filter and drill by period, hierarchy, horizon, and source while retaining the common population.
Missing stages and zero-denominator populations remain explicit in metrics, coverage, and exports.
Hand-calculated fixtures and browser tests prove the complete data-to-UI slice before additional stages are added.

title: Expand forecast value add across the full planning chain
what: Let planning leaders govern value added or destroyed across naive, statistical or ML, planner, commercial, consensus, and final approved forecast stages.
criteria: Configured planning stages appear in a deterministic business order and preserve stage, source, vintage, product, target, and horizon identity.
A value-add waterfall and stage table show accuracy, bias, absolute error, incremental value add, improved share, deterioration, and coverage at every stage.
Users can attribute stage transitions to available planner, team, function, hierarchy, or market actors without inventing missing ownership.
Late revisions and changes inside configured frozen horizons are separately measurable.
Stage comparisons support hierarchy, horizon, lifecycle, promotion, and forecastability segmentation when those dimensions are available.
Exports contain the exact aligned stage population and transition evidence.
Tests prevent averaging subgroup percentages or comparing unmatched stages.

title: Add governed demand-event context and segmentation
what: Let users place forecast performance alongside validated demand events and product characteristics while keeping observation separate from causal claims.
criteria: The data contract can ingest governed promotion, price, distribution, customer, lifecycle, launch, discontinuation, seasonality, supply-constraint, and lost-sales event records with provenance.
Users can filter or segment performance by available event and product characteristics without silently excluding unclassified observations.
Monthly and product-history charts can overlay event windows and source labels.
Exception and product detail views show relevant events as context with source, date, and confidence or status where supplied.
Interface copy describes association or context and never states that an event caused an error without a separately validated causal model.
Missing, overlapping, and conflicting event data remain visible in data trust diagnostics.
Tests cover event joins, duplicate prevention, period boundaries, and unchanged core metric populations.

title: Translate forecast exceptions into business impact
what: Prioritize forecast exceptions using optional validated revenue, margin, inventory, working-capital, waste, service, and lost-sales impact measures.
criteria: Business-impact inputs have explicit grain, currency, unit, effective-date, provenance, and missing-data contracts.
The queue can rank by configured business impact while retaining KL error and actual-volume evidence.
Over-forecast and under-forecast observations use distinct impact interpretations where validated inputs support them.
Missing commercial or supply inputs never generate fabricated impact values and remain visible as unavailable coverage.
The director cockpit shows top business risks and opportunities with the contributing metric and population.
Impact currency and aggregation rules are configurable for multi-market populations.
Hand-calculated fixtures and reconciliation exports prove every impact measure.

title: Reorganize the product around role-based planning workflows
what: Present the analytical foundation through role-appropriate planning workflows rather than one identical navigation hierarchy for every user.
criteria: The primary information architecture provides Executive cockpit, Performance diagnosis, Forecast value add, Exceptions and actions, Product deep dive, and Data trust destinations.
Directors land on target status, material risks, and open actions; planners land on their exception queue; data stewards land on remediation; model owners land on source comparison.
Role-specific defaults change presentation and landing location without changing metric definitions or silently narrowing authorized populations.
Forecast exceptions are removed from the Product history subview and become a dedicated workflow destination.
Technical provenance is moved out of permanent executive screen space into the governed lineage experience.
Navigation remains keyboard accessible, responsive, collapsible, history-aware, and shareable.
End-to-end browser suites cover every role and destination.

title: Add enterprise identity, permissions, and audit governance
what: Give enterprise customers authenticated access, governed visibility, accountable ownership, and an auditable record of user activity.
criteria: Users authenticate through a configurable enterprise SSO integration with a documented local-development alternative.
Role-based access controls govern populations, exports, workflow actions, administration, and sensitive business-impact data.
Ownership and comments use stable user identities rather than free-text names.
Security-relevant access, export, configuration, and workflow changes are recorded in an immutable audit log.
Data-retention and deletion policies are configurable and documented for analytical, workflow, and audit records.
Unauthorized data is not fetched or exposed through URLs, downloads, client state, or error messages.
Automated authorization and audit tests cover representative director, planner, data-steward, model-owner, and administrator roles.

title: Add scheduled reporting and governed integration APIs
what: Let authorized users distribute reproducible dashboard views and integrate governed forecast-performance data into enterprise workflows.
criteria: Users can schedule authorized saved views for email delivery and generate reproducible PDF and presentation-ready outputs.
Scheduled outputs include scope, metric definitions, refresh timestamp, data-current-through date, and coverage warnings.
A governed API exposes versioned metric, exception, quality, and workflow contracts with the same authorization rules as the UI.
Exports and API responses preserve exact active filters, aligned populations, units, and audit fields.
Delivery, refresh, and integration failures are monitored, retried according to policy, and visible to administrators.
Rate limits, pagination, schema versioning, and deprecation behavior are documented and tested.
No scheduled or API output can bypass row-level permissions or data-retention rules.

title: Add scenario comparison and decision tracking
what: Let planning teams compare named analytical scenarios, record a decision, and later evaluate whether the expected outcome was achieved.
criteria: Users can create named scenarios from saved scopes without mutating canonical forecast or actual data.
Two or more scenarios can be compared side by side with explicit differences in population, metrics, assumptions, and business impact.
A decision record captures selected scenario, owner, approver, rationale, expected impact, date, and linked exceptions or actions.
Decision status and approvals are permission-controlled and auditable.
When actuals become available, the product can compare realized outcome with the recorded expectation without asserting causality.
Scenario and decision links are shareable and remain reproducible against their saved input versions.
Tests cover stale inputs, conflicting updates, unauthorized approvals, and outcome follow-up.

title: Prove enterprise scale and operational readiness
what: Demonstrate that the product can be operated, secured, supported, and trusted at Fortune 500 portfolio scale.
criteria: Performance benchmarks cover agreed SKU-location-customer volumes, concurrent users, complex filters, charts, drill-through, exports, and scheduled jobs.
The system has defined service objectives for availability, refresh completion, interactive latency, export latency, and recovery.
Backup, restore, disaster recovery, deployment rollback, and schema migration procedures are tested with recorded evidence.
Security review covers authentication, authorization, secrets, dependencies, input validation, exports, APIs, and audit integrity.
Refresh, job, delivery, and application health are observable with actionable alerts and runbooks.
Release, environment, support, incident, and data-governance responsibilities are documented.
A production-readiness review reports measured pass, fail, and deferred outcomes rather than a blanket readiness claim.
